info.bio:
Big Star fue una banda estadounidense de Rock and Roll de la primera mitad de los 70. Formada en Memphis en el año de 1971, suele considerarse uno de los grupos precursores del power pop. Muy influenciada por el pop de los 60, y muy especialmente por grupos como The Beatles, The Byrds, The Kinks, The Zombies, Badfinger, The Who, Todd Rundgren, Moby Grape, The Beach Boys y Free. 

La música de Big Star es un pop lírico, enérgico y a veces nostálgico de la década precedente.

scenes.name: Pop de los setenta y power-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Abba, campeones del pop de los setenta, de las armonías efervescentes a la pista de baile y el melodrama romántico. Alex Chilton (Box Tops, Big Star) es el profeta del power-pop: melodía pura, armonías a cuatro voces, guitarras jingle-jangle y riffs de hard rock (Radio City); su ideología retro impregnará la new wave y el brit-pop de los noventa. Raspberries.

podcast.title: Commercial Flop, Critical Success
podcast.body: Big Star, with frontman Alex Chilton, aimed to follow in the footsteps of The Beatles and The Kinks while also admiring The Beach Boys' melodies. Despite being major critical darlings with a strong following among other musicians, they struggled with a bad record deal, failed to achieve hit singles, and sold few records, leading to their breakup after three years. "Unfortunately for Big Star, they couldn't manage any hit singles and never sold many records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Wave American Powerpop
podcast.body: Big Star, led by Alex Chilton, was recognized as one of the significant American bands during the first wave of power pop. "The Alex Chilton lead Big Star."

podcast.title: Influence on Modern Bands
podcast.body: Big Star's innovative sound influenced a wide range of bands, from The Cars and Blondie to Sloan and Blink-182, solidifying their legacy as foundational figures in Powerpop. "Someone from the cars in Blondie to Sloan and Blink 1.2 were influenced by Big Star."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

podcast.title: Musical Style - Melodic Hooks and Catchy Melodies
podcast.body: Big Star's genius lay in combining "very melodic hooks with very catchy melodies and big guitars," creating a sound that often appeared happy but frequently concealed lyrics that were "on the depressed and melancholy side." "But their genius was to combine very melodic hooks with very catchy melodies and big guitars. And while the music tended to sound happy, that often covered up lyrics that were on the depressed and melancholy side."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

podcast.title: Pioneers of Powerpop
podcast.body: From their formation in Memphis in 1971, Big Star is credited with essentially inventing the genre known as Powerpop, blending influences from The Beatles, The Who, and The Beach Boys with their own distinctive style. "They essentially invented the genre that we now call Powerpop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

podcast.title: Posthumous Rediscovery and Cult Following
podcast.body: After breaking up in 1975 due to commercial disappointment, Big Star was rediscovered in the 1990s by a new generation of alternative rock musicians and fans, leading to the development of a strong cult following. "But in the years that followed, especially in the 1990s, they were rediscovered by new generation of alt-wrong musicians and fans. A cult following built."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

podcast.title: Precursors to Other Powerpop Bands
podcast.body: Big Star predated other successful Powerpop bands of the 1970s, such as Badfinger, Todd Rundgren, The Raspberries, Cheap Trick, and The Knack, establishing the genre's foundation before its wider recognition. "There were other Powerpop bands in the 70s who had hits. There was Bad Finger and Todd Rungren. We had the raspberries, Cheap Trick, the Nack, but Big Star was there before all of them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

podcast.title: Reunion and Alex Chilton's Death
podcast.body: The band reunited in 1993 and remained active until singer Alex Chilton passed away from a heart attack, marking the end of their second phase. "A cult following built, and in 1993, the group reunited and stayed together until singer Alex Chilton died of a heart attack."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

podcast.title: Undiscovered Cult Favorite
podcast.body: After their breakup due to commercial struggles, Big Star remained an undiscovered cult favorite for approximately two decades. They were later "discovered" by a number of 90s-era alt-rock bands, who recognized that Big Star's sound from 1971 was significantly ahead of its time. "Big Star remained an undiscovered cult favorite for a couple of decades. But then they were discovered by a number of 90s era alt rock bands who realized that whatever Big Star was doing back in 1971, they were way, way ahead of their time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Career with The Box Tops (1967)
xref.body: As a 16-year-old, Alex Chilton served as the lead singer for The Box Tops, achieving a smash single with "The Letter" in the summer of 1967. After The Box Tops disbanded, Chilton went on to form Big Star. "Their frontman was Alex Chilton, who as a 16 year old kid, was the lead singer for the box tops on their summer of 67 Smash single The Letter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: American Influence
xref.body: The Beach Boys are revered by classic rock and pop fans and are noted for their melodies, which were admired by early Powerpop bands like Big Star. They represent an American counterpart to the British influences on Powerpop. "But we also have to give props to the so-called bubblegum sound of the 1960s and early 1970s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: British Invasion Influence
xref.body: The Kinks are cited as one of the British Invasion bands that followed The Beatles, further developing the sound that would lead to Powerpop. They are considered an influence by later Powerpop acts like Big Star. "Through the Beatles came all the rest of the British invasion bands, especially the Kinks and the Who."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Increased Stardom in Death
xref.body: Tupac (referred to as "Two Pock") was a big star when he was shot, but his fame and stature grew even larger in death. "And although two Pock and Big E were big stars when they were shot, they became even bigger stars in death."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Increased Stardom in Death
xref.body: Big E was already a big star when he was shot, but his fame and stature intensified significantly after his death. "And although two Pock and Big E were big stars when they were shot, they became even bigger stars in death."
